## Finishing

Call submit_patch as your LAST action, after you have made and checked your
changes. Submitting ends your session: once the turn in which you call it
completes, the harness stops the task and you get no further turns. Do not
call it after your first edit and expect to keep working.

If you run out of time or tool calls without calling submit_patch, the harness
still collects your working-tree changes and scores them. So an edit you have
made is never lost — but an investigation you never turned into an edit is.

## Committing to an edit

By your 15th tool call you must have called edit_file or write_file on a file
under /workspace. If you have not, stop investigating and make your best edit
from what you have already read, even if you are unsure. Then keep working:
refine it, check it, and submit at the end.

An empty patch scores zero. A wrong patch also scores zero and costs you
nothing. Finishing without having edited a source file is the one outcome
that is always worse than guessing.

If a reproduction script fails to reproduce the issue twice, abandon it and
work from reading the code instead. Do not rewrite it a third time.

Call get_status to see your remaining time and tool calls. It is free and does
not count against your budget.

## Scratch files

Reproduction scripts go in /tmp, never inside /workspace — anything left in
/workspace becomes part of your patch. Do not modify test files, conftest.py
or pytest.ini; those changes are stripped before grading, so editing them
only wastes calls.

## Scope

Most fixes in these repositories touch ONE file and change fewer than ten
lines. Modify existing code rather than adding new code. Do not refactor,
reformat, or make unrelated changes. If your patch is growing past a few
files, stop and reconsider the diagnosis.

Exception: if the issue asks for functionality that does not exist yet,
create the file or function it describes, and match any names, CLI flags
or interfaces the issue specifies exactly.

## Finding the code

A truncated result loses information silently, so a broad read wastes a call
and leaves you guessing. Narrow before you read:

  run_command("grep -rln '<symbol>' --include='*.py' .")       # files only
  run_command("grep -n '<symbol>' path/to/one_file.py")        # then inside one

Use -l to find the file, then -n only within that file. Read with read_file on
a tight line range around the match. Never read a whole file and never cat
one — you will get an arbitrary prefix and burn the call.

async def solve_dependencies(
    *,
    request: Union[Request, WebSocket],
    dependant: Dependant,
    body: Optional[Union[Dict[str, Any], FormData]] = None,
    background_tasks: Optional[StarletteBackgroundTasks] = None,
    response: Optional[Response] = None,
    dependency_overrides_provider: Optional[Any] = None,
    dependency_cache: Optional[Dict[DependencyCacheKey, Any]] = None,
    # TODO: remove this parameter later, no longer used, not removing it yet as some
    # people might be monkey patching this function (although that's not supported)
    async_exit_stack: AsyncExitStack,
    embed_body_fields: bool,
) -> SolvedDependency:
    request_astack = request.scope.get("fastapi_inner_astack")
    assert isinstance(request_astack, AsyncExitStack), (
        "fastapi_inner_astack not found in request scope"
    )
    function_astack = request.scope.get("fastapi_function_astack")
    assert isinstance(function_astack, AsyncExitStack), (
        "fastapi_function_astack not found in request scope"
    )
    values: Dict[str, Any] = {}
    errors: List[Any] = []
    if response is None:
        response = Response()
        del response.headers["content-length"]
        response.status_code = None  # type: ignore
    if dependency_cache is None:
        dependency_cache = {}
    for sub_dependant in dependant.dependencies:
        sub_dependant.call = cast(Callable[..., Any], sub_dependant.call)
        call = sub_dependant.call
        use_sub_dependant = sub_dependant
        if (
            dependency_overrides_provider
            and dependency_overrides_provider.dependency_overrides
        ):
            original_call = sub_dependant.call
            call = getattr(
                dependency_overrides_provider, "dependency_overrides", {}
            ).get(original_call, original_call)
            use_path: str = sub_dependant.path  # type: ignore
            use_sub_dependant = get_dependant(
                path=use_path,
                call=call,
                name=sub_dependant.name,
                security_scopes=sub_dependant.security_scopes,
                scope=sub_dependant.scope,
            )

        solved_result = await solve_dependencies(
            request=request,
            dependant=use_sub_dependant,
            body=body,
            background_tasks=background_tasks,
            response=response,
            dependency_overrides_provider=dependency_overrides_provider,
            dependency_cache=dependency_cache,
            async_exit_stack=async_exit_stack,
            embed_body_fields=embed_body_fields,
        )
        background_tasks = solved_result.background_tasks
        if solved_result.errors:
            errors.extend(solved_result.errors)
            continue
        if sub_dependant.use_cache and sub_dependant.cache_key in dependency_cache:
            solved = dependency_cache[sub_dependant.cache_key]
        elif (
            use_sub_dependant.is_gen_callable or use_sub_dependant.is_async_gen_callable
        ):
            use_astack = request_astack
            if sub_dependant.scope == "function":
                use_astack = function_astack
            solved = await _solve_generator(
                dependant=use_sub_dependant,
                stack=use_astack,
                sub_values=solved_result.values,
            )
        elif use_sub_dependant.is_coroutine_callable:
            solved = await call(**solved_result.values)
        else:
            solved = await run_in_threadpool(call, **solved_result.values)
        if sub_dependant.name is not None:

        if sub_dependant.cache_key not in dependency_cache:

from fastapi import FastAPI, Depends, Security
from fastapi.security import OAuth2PasswordBearer
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from fastapi.dependencies.utils import solve_dependencies
from fastapi.dependencies.models import Dependant
import pytest

app = FastAPI()
oauth2_scheme = OAuth2PasswordBearer(tokenUrl="token")

def dep_c(security_scopes: SecurityScopes = Security(oauth2_scheme, scopes=["scope1"])):
    return "C"

def dep_b(c=Depends(dep_c)):
    return f"B({c})"

def dep_a(b=Depends(dep_b)):
    return f"A({b})"

@app.get("/")
def read_root(a=Depends(dep_a)):
    return a

# This is a simplified test. I'll use TestClient to see if it works.
# But I need to check if the cache is actually working.
# Since I cannot easily inspect the internal cache of FastAPI during a request,
# I might need to use a mock or a side effect.

def dep_c_side_effect(security_scopes: SecurityScopes = Security(oauth2_scheme, scopes=["scope1"])):
    dep_c_side_effect.count += 1
    return "C"
dep_c_side_effect.count = 0

def dep_b_side_effect(c=Depends(dep_c_side_effect)):
    dep_b_side_effect.count += 1
    return f"B({c})"
dep_b_side_effect.count = 0

def dep_a_side_effect(b=Depends(dep_b_side_effect)):
    dep_a_side_effect.count += 1
    return f"A({b})"
dep_a_side_effect.count = 0

@app.get("/test")
def test_endpoint(a=Depends(dep_a_side_effect)):
    return a

client = TestClient(app)

def test_cache():
    # First request
    client.get("/test", headers={"Authorization": "Bearer token1"})
    # First request should call a, b, c once
    assert dep_a_side_effect.count == 1
    assert dep_b_side_effect.count == 1
    assert dep_c_side_effect.count == 1

    # Actually, the dependency cache is per request in solve_dependencies.
